output:
I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data.

The middle of the rules was cut off. I'll read it in full.

I wrote `/app/bin/payroll.py` and ran it on `/app/data`. The result is saved as `/app/out/payroll.json`. `python3 /app/tools/check_payroll.py` printed "OK: every value matches the approved figures." All 150 employees match on every field, and the exception counts and totals match too.

The script uses only the standard library and takes about 10 seconds on this data. It reads all nine export formats and follows the rules in `payroll-rules.md`.

I only ran it on the current period. The other-period cases are covered only by following the docs, such as clocks going back, gzip files and header changes inside a file.

If the same site and punch id arrives twice with different contents, the script keeps the first one it reads. The docs don't say what to do in that case.

I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | head -100; cat docs/payroll-rules.md docs/exports.md docs/output.md
cd /app; ls data data/corrections tools; ls data/exports; cat data/sites.csv data/period.json; head -5 data/employees.csv data/rates.csv; python3 tools/check_payroll.py --help | head -20

cd /app; cat tools/check_payroll.py | head -60; head -c 600 tools/reference-digests.json; for s in data/exports/*; do echo == $s; ls $s | wc -l; f=$(ls $s/* | head -1); file $f; head -c 400 $f; done; head -5 data/corrections/batch-1.csv

cd /app; sed -n 60,200p tools/check_payroll.py; cat data/corrections/*.csv | awk -F, '{print $3}' | sort | uniq -c; grep -h -v '^C0' data/corrections/*.csv | head; cd data/exports; python3 - <<'E'
import glob,gzip
n=0
for f in glob.glob('*/*'):
    b=open(f,'rb').read()
    if b[:2]==b'\x1f\x8b': n+=1
    if b'\xef\xbb\xbf' in b[:3]: print('bom',f)
print('gz',n)
E
grep -l '^H' kiln/* | head -3; grep -h '^H' kiln/* | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
cd /app; python3 -V; python3 -c "import zoneinfo;print(zoneinfo.ZoneInfo('Asia/Kathmandu'))"; ls bin out 2>&1; grep -c . data/employees.csv data/rates.csv

cd /app/data/exports; grep -h '^H' kiln/* | awk '{print length($0)}' | sort | uniq -c; grep -l 'HKILN.*+' kiln/* | head -3; python3 - <<'E'
import glob
for f in glob.glob('*/*'):
    b=open(f,'rb').read()
    if b[:2]==b'\x1f\x8b': print(f)
E
grep -h Badge harbor-point/* southbank/* | sort | uniq -c

cd /app/data/exports; grep -n -B1 -A3 '^HKILN.*+' kiln/KILN261010.DAT | head -20; grep -c . kiln/KILN261010.DAT; grep -n '^[HT]' kiln/KILN261010.DAT; python3 -c "import sys;print(open('kiln/KILN261010.DAT','rb').read()[-120:])"; grep -h -A2 Badge harbor-point/* | grep -v ',T' | head; grep -h ':[0-9][0-9],' harbor-point/* | awk -F, '{print $4}' | grep -v 'M$' | head -3

cd /app; python3 - <<'E'
p='bin/payroll.py'
s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index('            yield str(o["punch_id"])'):s.index('        else:\n            if "id" not in o')]
s=s.replace(old,'            yield str(o["punch_id"]), o["employee"], norm_dir(o["direction"]), \\\n                math.floor(Decimal(str(o["epoch_ms"])) / 1000)\n')
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json && python3 tools/check_payroll.py
cd /app; sed -i 's/tz.fromutc(utc_from_epoch(\([a-z]*\)))/utc_from_epoch(\1).astimezone(tz)/' bin/payroll.py; grep -n 'astimezone(tz)\|fromutc' bin/payroll.py; wc -l bin/payroll.py
cd /app; sed -n 1,20p bin/payroll.py | cat -A | head -20; python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json && python3 tools/check_payroll.py

cd /app; echo '{"status": "success", "summary": "Wrote /app/bin/payroll.py (stdlib only) implementing all documented formats and rules, ran it on /app/data to produce /app/out/payroll.json; tools/check_payroll.py reports every value matches the approved figures."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
